3. Fact relevant for disposal of this Rule in short are that some people living in the locality, near the "Sultanshi Abasik Area" under Habigonj Sadar, District-Habigonj are threatening the general people of that area and thereby forcing them to obey the "Fatwa" regarding wearing/using caps, shoes and umbrellas while crossing a particular place through the road which is passing through the said particular area of Sultanshi. It is stated that the petitioner along with others of the said locality filed an application to all the respondents stating that some "Fatwabaz" are threatening and creating obstruction to the normal movement of the villagers while crossing a particular place/area on foot using the road towards Sultanshi, upon wearing shoes, caps and using umbrellas. It is also stated that the said road is not a private road rather a public road constructed by the funds of the LGRD. The said restriction has been imposed upon the local people specially during the Arabic month of "Muharram" while a particular group of people organize religious programme at Village-Loskarpur under Hobigonj Sadar Police Station which is situated near the Sultanshi Residential Area. It is further stated that the road passing through the said village/area is used by all the common people of the locality but during the month of Muharram some organizers create obstruction to the normal movement of the people restricting using of shoes, caps and umbrellas while passing through the said area/village. Such news has been published in the daily newspaper and the petitioner having felt that the fundamental right of the citizen to enjoy their right to religion and free movement are being infringed by such restriction imposed by a group of people as such applications have been filed to the authority for reddres. Having received no action from the respondents pursuant to such applications, the petitioner filed this writ petition for redress on the ground that imposition of such restriction is violative of Articles 28, 31, 36 and 41 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. The Office Secretary of the "Holy Ashura Udzapon Committee," Sultanshi Habeli, Village Sultanshi, .added itself as Respondent No.9 in this writ petition who filed affidavit in opposition denying the material allegations made in the writ petition, contending inter alia that the followers of Islam, who observe Holy Ashura and other connected religious functions from 1st to 10th of Muharram, like bringing out "Tazia Missil" and "Marsia" to recall the memory of Karbala and to show respect to the souls of the martyrs of Karbala, including Hazrat Imam Hussain (R), within the "Sultanshi Habeli" area (lmambara), deliberately refrain themselves from using shoes, caps and umbrellas in that area, and no one is ever compelled to and no fatwa has ever been made restricting the people to attend the function using shoes, caps, and umbrellas. It is the willful act of the general public while attending the function and it is a long standing practice, tradition and custom of all the "Imambaras" in the Muslim World. The respondent No. 9 also supported the statements of the respondent No. 4 regarding holding of meeting on 18-5-2003 by the local elites and the decision taken therein that no restriction be imposed on using caps, shoes and umbrellas during Ashura or Muharram time. It is further contended that the petitioner is a motivated person of the locality involved in drug trafficking and using drugs and narcotics and he raised objection to such activities only to create obstruction in performing Ashura from 1st to 10th Muharram and accordingly on 10-5-2012 the Local Union Parishad Chairman took a. decision that temporary signboard may be put up requesting the followers of Ashura not to use caps, shoes and umbrellas in the Imambara on first 10 day of Muharram which is to be removed from the said place after 10th Moharram. He denied the allegation that the organizers threatened the general people and creates obstruction to the normal movement of the villagers using shoes, caps and umbrellas rather the people of the locality are using the said road very peacefully without any obstruction or hindrance from anybody. It is also alleged that the petitioner does not reside at his birth place, Sultanshi, nor he is a voter of that place. He is a permanent resident of Sylhet city where he is involved in several criminal activities as evident from National Dailies for which he was arrested by the Police and RAB on several occasions. It is further contended that "Shaheb Bari" is a private property and the road in question is situated on the west side of the Imambara and the Dorgah Sharif of the Shaheb Bari complex, which has been developed by the funds of the LGRD in 2003 and the Dorgah Complex has also been developed during that time with the co-operation of the LGRD. The 450 meters road connecting "Dhulia Khal" and "Kotiadi" situated on the west side of the Imambara and Dorgah Sharif, mutated in the name of the Shaeb Bari, has been constructed jointly by the LGRD and Ashura and Dorgah Committee. Upon annexing a copy of the report of the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet, the said respondent contended that the said report clearly shows that 'no signboard is found in existence in and around the area as alleged by the petitioner and upon examining the people of the locality it has been found that the function and program of Muharram is organized by "Muharram udzapon Committee", who since 2003, temporarily puts up the signboard/notice restricting using of caps, shoes and umbrellas only for a period of 10 days from 1st to 10th Muharram and, as such, there is no restriction on the common people to use cap, shoe and umbrella beyond the "Imambara compound". The said respondent No.9 in its affidavit made certain allegations which are denied by the petitioner as such the same being disputed questions of fact are not required to be stated for the disposal of this Rule. 

 6. It appears from the record that pursuant to order dated 26-11-2012 the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet upon investigating the matter prepared a report on 3-1-2013 which has been sent to the Registrar of the Supreme Court on 25-11-2013 (Annexures XI to the affidavit in opposition by the respondent No.9). The contents of which has already been stated hereinabove. 

 11. Upon referring to some annexures appended to the affidavit in opposition filed by respondent No.9, Mr Monzill Murshed claims that the road is not the private road of "Imambara" as evident from Annexure-D-I and the "Porch a" annexed to Annexure-D-I wherefrom it is clear that the Road belongs to the government. Referring to Annexure-D-3 to the said affidavit Mr Monzill Morshed submits that objection has been raised under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules in respect of recording of some part of the road in the name of Imambara which is pending. As such the respondent No.9 cannot claim the property to be "Imambara's absolute private property. Referring to the report of the Divisional Commissioner he submits that 3.8 Kilometer Road from "Dhuliakhal Kutiadi Bazar" to "Sultanshi Mazar Road" having ID No. 636444036 has been constructed by the funds of the LGED in 2003-2004 including 450 Meters pavement adjacent to the said Mazar Road and the said road is used by the general public. As such MrMorshed submits that the claim of the respondent No.9 that the road belongs to the "Imambara" is not correct at all, rather the same is a disputed question of fact and unless the same is finally decided by the appropriate authority/competent court the respondent No.9 cannot claim the same to be Imambara's private property. As such imposition of any restriction on such property is illegal. 

 13. On this backdrop we have perused the writ petition, affidavit in oppositions, supplementary affidavit in oppositions, affidavit in reply and also the papers annexed thereto. It is clear from the submission of the respondents as well as from the report of the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet that from 1 st to 10th Muharram some followers of Islam gather in the "Imamabara" to observe the rituals of Muharram and participate in "TaziaMissil", "Marsia" procession etc. and in the said gathering the people generally do not wear caps, shoes and umbrellas within the "Imambara area", voluntarily, to pay respect to the departed souls of the Martyrs of the Karbala. From the papers placed before us and the report of the Divisional Commissioner it is clear that no restriction is imposed upon any person in respect of wearing shoe, cap and umbrella. It is specifically admitted by the respondent No.9 that no such restriction has been imposed upon the people who are using the said road. Thus it appears that the people while gathering "within the Imambara complex" voluntarily do not wear/ use shoes, caps, and umbrellas. Since from the statements made by all the respondents that admittedly there is no such restriction upon wearing and using of such articles while crossing the road towards the "Sultanshi Residential Area" rather the people voluntarily do not use the same within the "Imambara" area which is the private property, we do not find any reason to interfere with the matter so long such restriction is not imposed beyond the private property of the "Imambara". 

 14. But fact remains if such restriction is imposed beyond the "Imambara" area, which is admittedly not the private property of the "Imambara", then question comes whether interference of this court. is required? It is claimed by the respondent No. 9 that such restriction is made only for 1st 10 days in the month of Moharram within the "Imambara" but simultaneously the said respondent also claims that such signboard in the form of notice is put on the 450 meter connecting road which is the private property of Imambara. From the materials on record it appears that the said 450 meter road is claimed by respondent No. 9 to be Imambara's property used as connecting road running towards the "Sultanshi Residential Area" But the petitioner claims that the said road is not the private property of the "Imambara" as appear from Annexures D(2) to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner, which shows that the same is under Khatian No.1 recorded not in the name of Imambara but in the name of the Government of Bangladesh., It further appears that a case is pending before the authority under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules which is also admitted by respondent No. 9 as well as by the respondent No.4. On the other hand the respondent No.3 in his report stated that 'no restriction or embargo has been made/ imposed upon any person beyond the area of the "Imambara" area. Thus we are of the view that the temporary sign board, as evident from the photographs (Annexure- B series to the writ petition) captioning সরকারী নির্দেশ মোতাবেক পবিত্র মহরমের নিয়মাবলির প্রতি শ্রদ্ধা জ্ঞাপনর্থে ইমাম বাড়ায় নিজস্ব রাত্তা দিয়ে চলাচলের সময় সকলকে জুতা টুপি ও ছাতা ব্যবহার না করার জন্য অনুরোধ করা হইল। clearly show that the same has been put up beside the road which runs towards the "Sultanshi Residential Area" which is con- fusing. Neither the respondent No.3 nor the respondent No.4 in their reports or in the affidavit admits that the government has given such direction or permission upon the "Muharram Udzapon Committee" to hang/ put up such sign board under the said caption. However, since the signboard if any, is put up on the private property of the respondent No. 9 and since there in no embargo in putting such signboard/notice on the private property the same cannot/does not create any embargo upon the pedestrian generally using the public road running towards "Sultanshi Residential Area", upon wearing caps, shoes and umbrellas. In respect of putting up such sign- board/notice on the 450 meter road immaterial whether the same is claimed to be the private road of the "Imambara" or the same belongs to the government (as appears from Annexure-D(2) to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner showing that the LGED has constructed the said road) and that a miscellaneous case under Rule 30 of the SA &T Rules is pending before the appropriate authority, thus it is clear that there are disputes in respect of the said road/property in question. As such, no such notice or signboard can be put up thereon unless the miscellaneous case under Rules is disposed of or upon finally deciding the title in an appropriate suit by the civil court. However, till finalization of the matter of owner ships of the said road the respondent No.9 or anyone else, cannot under any circumstances, put up such sign board.
